text.p: These are the leading stories in the Angolan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Rebel Unita leader Jonas Savimbi has declined an invitation to travel from his central stronghold to the government-controlled capital Luanda to meet U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher on his stop-over in Angola on Monday.

- Unita leader Jonas Savimbi has proposed for himself a special political status as opposition leader in a future unity government, a document handed to the government by Unita representatives in Luanda said.
- The United Nations Security Council, debating the U.N. peacekeeping mandate in Angola, said it was worried about the lack of progress in the Angolan peace process to end two decades of civil war.
